text:
taylor: Heads-up — saw a p99 tail spike on the model pool after yesterday's kernel repack. Not a full outage but p99 up ~2.5x during short bursts. Collecting notes here so we can triage.

sanjay: saw it too on the dashboard. p95 steady, but p99 jumps for ~30s windows.

maya: timeline? did this align w/ rollout of the new fused-attn kernels?

taylor: yes, new kernels went live ~21:12 UTC. Metrics: baseline (pre-rollout) at 50rps: p95 120ms p99 420ms. After rollout peaks: p95 140ms p99 1050ms for short periods.

rafa: interesting — the histogram shows a secondary mode at ~2s. That's usually queue jitter + kv cold misses compounded. Can you paste qlen and kv hit traces?

taylor: pasting trimmed profiler snippets below. note: these are from a single affected instance.

```
# top-level timeline (sampled)
100ms  - dispatch + kernel select
60ms   - wait (batching queue)
30ms   - kernel exec
+ cache: 0/10 hits
=> total ~190ms

# during tail
150ms  - dispatch + kernel select
600ms  - wait (queue jitter)  <-- big
120ms  - kernel exec (slightly faster)
+ cache: 1/10 hits
=> total ~870ms
```

sanjay: queue waiting ballooned. Any change in `max_batch_tokens` or scheduling policy?

taylor: no config change; runtime used the new kernel variant which prefers larger microbatches and defers kernel fallback for a bit. Hypothesis: kernel selection prefers fusable kernel which increases preferred batch token target, so scheduler waits longer to fill batches. That increases tail for low-concurrency microbursts.

maya: that matches. We saw similar when we tuned for throughput: better avg throughput but worse tail on bursty traffic. Could be compounded by KV cache churn — low hit rate -> more token requests -> longer assembly time.

rafa: propose quick experiments (A/B):
- A: reduce `max_batch_tokens` on the pool from 8192 -> 4096, keep `max_wait_ms` at 12.
- B: keep `max_batch_tokens` at 8192, reduce `max_wait_ms` from 12 -> 6.
- C: enable early-fallback to generic kernel when wait >= 8ms.

sanjay: +1. Also track per-request KV hit-rate and `dispatch.wait_ms` histogram. Need consistent profiling tag to correlate kernel choice and kv status.

taylor: I can run A and B on a canary zone for 30m each. C needs runtime flag change; might be slightly riskier but we can test in staging.

dev-bot: rollout plan created: canary: pool-us-east-3a, 10% traffic. Health checks: p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_avg, dispatch_wait_p90.

maya: add a synthetic burst test too — 200 rps for 10s with real prompt mix to reproduce microburst behavior. That helped reveal tails previously.

taylor: results from quick canary A (max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=12):
- avg batch size down from 7.8k tokens -> 4.1k tokens
- p95: 130ms (unchanged)
- p99: 460ms -> 330ms (nice improvement)
- throughput: -6% during steady load
- observed KV hit-rate: +2% (small bump)

rafa: good win on tail. What about B (keep batch tokens high, lower wait ms)?

sanjay: B results (max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=6):
- avg batch size ~6.9k tokens
- p95: 125ms
- p99: 380ms
- throughput: -2%

taylor: so B recovered some tail without as big throughput hit as A. C (early fallback) not yet tested in prod.

maya: curious about kernel exec times — did new fused kernel exec time go down enough to offset queue wait?

taylor: kernel execs slightly faster (~10% lower median), but not enough when queue waits balloon. So key is bounding wait.

rafa: also looked at per-model routing: heavier prompts with long kv sequences had lower cache hit rate which made them more likely to be in the tail. Can we prioritize requests with warm kv? Maybe route warm-kv requests to the fused kernel queue and cold to generic kernel slot?

sanjay: we could add a dispatch heuristic: if kv_hit_estimate < 0.3 then prefer immediate generic kernel; else allow aggregation for fused kernel. Need experiment.

taylor: sketch of heuristic (pseudo):

```
if kv_estimated_hit < 0.3:
  dispatch.max_wait_ms = 2  # fast-path
  dispatch.prefer_kernel = "generic"
else:
  dispatch.max_wait_ms = global_max_wait
  dispatch.prefer_kernel = "fused"
```

maya: nice. That hybrid approach might recover throughput while bounding tail. Could also add a soft cap: if queue length > 30 requests, force fallback.

dev-bot: synthetic burst test scheduled. Canary B will be promoted to 30% if p99 stays < 420ms for 1h.

taylor: next steps I propose:
1) Roll B to 10% (done), run synthetic burst, collect `dispatch.wait_ms` heatmap + kernel selection tag.
2) Prototype kv-aware dispatch heuristic in staging.
3) If stable, promote B to 30% and run C in staging.

rafa: add a long-term item: autoscale scheduling policy based on observed request-size distribution per minute. If median seq_len > X, bias toward larger batch tokens. If burstiness metric > Y, reduce wait_ms.

sanjay: agree. I'll open a perf-research ticket with these experiments and link traces.

maya: thanks everyone — this feels actionable. taylor, can you drop the canary logs in the ticket after the burst test?

taylor: will do. dropping a quick reproduction command for others to run locally:

```
# burst generator (simple)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/generate -d '{"prompt":"story...","max_tokens":256}' &
done
wait
```

rafa: FYI, leaving a note: keep an eye on cold-start kernel compilation on hosts — compilation latencies can add to tail if kernel not resident. We should preload top-3 kernels on boot.

taylor: noted. ok closing thread for now, will update thread_ts when canary logs uploaded. :thumbsup:
